newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent, gas oil settle sharply up on Iraq moves.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent, gas oil settle sharply up on Iraq moves.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures settled at a five-year high on Monday, while Brent crude traded at its highest level since mid-April just before the close, spurred by tension in northern Iraq and a delay in Iraqi oil exports.

October Brent futures soared to $22 a barrel just before the close of a shortened trading session on the IPE because of the U.S. Labor Day holiday. The front month last traded up $1.21 at $21.99 a barrel.
Late interest with some buying from U.S. customers supported the London market and pushed gas oil to a five-year high of $207.50 a tonne, up $11 on the day.
"Technically we are headline driven in a thin and volatile market," said Charles Gray of the energy desk at Prudential Bache Futures in a report.
He added that on the technical charts, there was a total vacuum to the year's high of $23 a barrel if October Brent broke through the next resistance level of $22.05.

Monday's rally began after traders arrived at their desks to the news that the United Nations had postponed its oil-for-food deal with Iraq following the incursion of Iraqi troops into Iraqi Kurdistan in support of a Kurdish faction.

The market had anticipated that limited Iraqi oil sales, which have been banned by a U.N. embargo imposed after Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990, would resume some time in September under a deal allowing Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil to buy food and medicines.
The White House dismissed as insignificant Iraq's reported withdrawal of troops from the Kurdish stronghold of Arbil because Iraqi forces remained outside the city.
